candidate.cv_text:
Sarah Chen
Software Engineer → Product Manager

Experience

Product Manager, Growth — Stripe (2022–present)
- Led redesign of the merchant onboarding flow, reducing time-to-first-payment from 14 days to 3 days for SMB customers
- Shipped a risk-scoring feature used by fraud ops team, reducing manual review queue by 40%
- Partnered with 3 engineering teams and legal to navigate PCI compliance changes; launched on schedule across 12 markets
- Managed a portfolio of 6 concurrent initiatives; defined quarterly OKRs for a team of 11

Software Engineer, Platform — Atlassian (2019–2022)
- Designed and owned the Jira notification routing service, processing 200M events/day
- Reduced p99 latency from 1.2s to 180ms through async processing and queue redesign
- Led a 4-person team through a 6-month deprecation of a legacy routing pipeline; zero downtime migration
- Mentored 2 junior engineers; one promoted to mid within 18 months

Software Engineer — Canva (2017–2019)
- Built the export pipeline for design-to-PDF rendering; reduced export failure rate from 12% to 0.8%
- Part of the team that scaled infrastructure from 5M to 30M users during hypergrowth phase

Education
Bachelor of Computer Science, University of Sydney, 2017

Skills: Python, Go, SQL, product strategy, roadmap management, stakeholder communication, data analysis

role.title: Senior Product Manager
role.context: Growth team at a Series B fintech building embedded payments infrastructure for marketplaces

company_profile.behavioral_style: structured; expects STAR answers with quantified impact, systems-level thinking, and clear articulation of personal contribution vs. team contribution
company_profile.tempo: brisk — moves quickly if answer is shallow; slows down to probe when something interesting surfaces
company_profile.base_rigor: high — expects precise language, measurable outcomes, and clear disambiguation of individual vs. team work
company_profile.hint_tolerance: very low — never offers hints; silence after a weak answer is expected
company_profile.followup_style: drill-down — follows a single thread to its depth before moving on; probes for edge cases and tradeoffs
company_profile.notes: FAANG-style behavioral interviews operate on Leadership Principles or equivalent frameworks. Expects candidates to own their narrative, quantify impact, and demonstrate comfort with ambiguity. Shallow answers will surface follow-ups that feel uncomfortable.

signals: Has shaped direction, not just executed against it
Drives outcomes across teams or functions
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and making calls without full information
Demonstrates investment in others' growth (mentorship, unblocking, sponsorship)
Impact is systemic — changes processes, norms, or culture, not just delivers projects
red_flags: Impact is still described at the individual-contribution level
No examples of influencing upward or across without formal authority
Struggles to describe ambiguous or underdefined situations they navigated
People development is absent from their narrative
Overly credits team for everything — ownership is unclear
evaluation.seniority_note: 6+ years expected. Senior candidates should demonstrate leverage — their work makes other people and systems more effective. Look for multiplier behaviours: mentorship, cross-functional influence, process improvement, and strategic input.
